A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFOS research, with matching authors, algorithms, experiments, and Appendices A–F. The text, equations, and figures support reliable comparison despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations on six optimal-stopping problems, finite-agent approximation experiments, and learning-rate sweeps in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and analyses in Section 6 and Appendices E–F, including the finite-agent comparison in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The direct and dynamic-programming algorithms retain their optimization steps, losses, population-dependent network inputs, and architectures. Their short pseudocodes exchange numbers, but neither procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six environments, including congestion, distribution matching, and drones with common-noise obstacles. The new motivating example reformulates the existing distributional-cost example rather than adding evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: The DA/DP comparisons and analytical optimal-cost references are retained in corresponding experiments. Newly cited methods are discussed as related work, without additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: State spaces, horizons, initial distributions, congestion coefficient, noise settings, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The congestion transition formula moves to Appendix E.3 with the same values.

E4.justification: Both retain synchronous/asynchronous comparisons, finite-agent scaling, tests with different initial distributions, and Appendix F's learning-rate sweep. Reorganized appendix plots contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: The finite-agent distribution errors and cost gaps are averaged over 10 runs in both versions. No changed seed information, repeated-run procedure, confidence interval, or significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: All experimental plots from v1 are retained with identical plotted content, although panels are moved or regrouped. The finite-agent convergence curves and Example 2's reported optimal values of 1.6525 and 3.25 remain unchanged; the introductory drone illustration summarizes existing results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 revises Lemma A.1's error propagation to include geometric accumulation of sampling errors and updates Theorem A.3's explicit bound. The O(N^-1/2) rate and DPP remain unchanged. v2 also explicitly states terminal stopping; several policy formulas drop distribution arguments despite retaining them elsewhere, leaving some inconsistency.

C1.justification: The central approximation, DPP, two-algorithm, and scalability contributions remain. However, v2 drops the introduction's explicit claim of handling much higher dimensions than prior discrete-time MFC reinforcement-learning work and refocuses the conclusion's computational-gap claim on difficulties adapting single-agent OS methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of cooperative stopping tradeoffs and why treating the population as one stopping agent misses the intended interactions. It explicitly identifies continuous-space extension as future work and removes v1's Remark 2.3 discussion of different agent policies and their vanishing optimality gap.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the network architecture, AdamW learning rate of 10^-4, batch size 128, maximum 10^4 iterations, RTX 4090/M2 hardware, and runtime information. No new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens the literature discussion to PDE, BSDE, deep-learning, and reinforcement-learning approaches for MFC. It adds MFOS references including Yu and Yuan, Agram and Øksendal, and He, and expands the positioning against single-agent OS methods, including Tsitsiklis and Van Roy.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and substantially revises its introductory narrative, motivation, and concluding exposition. It adds a motivating example and challenges block, promotes the approximation discussion from Section 2.4 to Section 3, and condenses and redistributes experimental descriptions.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, adds overview Figures 1–2 and highlighted statement boxes, and extensively rearranges existing figures. Loss panels move into the appendices, some comparisons are merged, and the 2D examples and learning-rate sweeps receive much larger displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves Appendix A's treatment of accumulated sampling error and makes the paper easier to follow through clearer motivation, broader research context, and more legible appendix plots. The algorithms and empirical evidence remain unchanged. Some inconsistent policy notation persists or is introduced, limiting the theoretical cleanup, but the documented corrections and presentation gains support a modest overall improvement.
